annotations.annotation_text: Oneiric dimension "night" on page 329 ("The Tavern"): the nocturnal consciousness surfaces within HCE behind the bar at his Chapelizod pub, the Norwegian Captain tale, the television broadcast, the twelve customers drinking and judging. During this Age of Heroes phase, Joyce reconstructs the sleeping body's sensory deprivation — dimmed sight, distorted hearing, dream-logic association — transforming somatic experience into polyphonic language.
sources: Bishop, John. Joyce's Book of the Dark. https://archive.org/details/joycesbookofdark0000bish
Freud, Sigmund. The Interpretation of Dreams. https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/4349
Troy, Mark L. Mummeries of Resurrection. http://www.rosenlake.net

annotations.annotation_text: Issy/daughter figure "daughter" on page 329 ("The Tavern"): the narcissistic mirror-daughter, modeled on Isolde and Swift's dual muses Stella and Vanessa, appears here within HCE behind the bar at his Chapelizod pub, the Norwegian Captain tale, the television broadcast, the twelve customers drinking and judging. Her prismatic splitting into twenty-eight Rainbow Girls reflects the cycle's Age of Heroes phase through youthful seduction and self-reflection.
sources: Bédier, Joseph. The Romance of Tristan and Iseult. https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/14244
Tindall, William York. A Reader's Guide to Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/readersguidetofi00tind
